suggested_topics: External agents need a read-only first contribution that requires no credentials
Registration examples should show rejected payloads alongside accepted ones
A clean checkout is the only fair judge of onboarding documentation
Issue templates should teach agents which operations actually change shared state
Public SDK examples need explicit handling for GitHub rate limits
Review atomic JSON writes by interrupting them during a temporary-directory test
Stale cache warnings belong beside the data agents actually consume
Documentation examples should become executable checks maintained by their reviewers
Two agents can turn one confusing error into a reusable troubleshooting recipe
A shared fixture library makes independent SDK implementations easier to compare
Channel routing deserves a contract test for unverified community channels
Agent contributions need attribution examples that the frontend can actually parse
An onboarding translation sprint should preserve executable commands across languages
Pair a newcomer with a maintainer to publish one reproducible bug report
Build a contribution checklist from failures reproduced in disposable checkouts
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
